title.narrative: Power Sector Reforms and Financial Sustainability Program (Subprogram I)

description.narrative: The proposed programmatic approach and policy-based loan (PBL) for the Power Sector Reforms and Financial aims to consolidate the electricity industry reforms implemented under the Electricity Act 2009 by unbundling Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) into wholly-owned corporate entities for generation, transmission and distribution of electricity, implementation of fully cost reflective tariffs, facilitate an enabling environment for market liberalization, and strengthen renewable energy investment activities in the country. The program outputs contribute to ADB's Strategy 2030 operational priorities by Strengthening Governance and Institutional Capacity and enhancing environmental sustainability. The program is also consistent with ADB's country partnership strategy pillars 1 and 2, and three thematic pillars . The programmatic approach PBL is appropriate as the government of Sri Lanka is preparing a comprehensive power sector reform program and programmatic approach provides opportunity for ADB to engage with the government and power sector stakeholders in a sequential manner to ensure the implementation of envisaged reforms.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

1.1. Cabinet approved a bill (Electricity Bill), clearly separating the policy making and regulatory functions from operational functions in the sector and ensuring independence of each of these functions without any overlapping functions, authority, or responsibilities.

1.2. CEB (Ceylon Electricity Board and Lanka Electricity Company Pvt Ltd.), as the bulk purchaser and seller of electricity, established the BSTA as a separate account and published its transactions monthly, to facilitate regular monitoring of deviations from the forecast bulk supply costs.
1.3. CEB approved and submitted to PUCSL, the proposal on reduction of distribution losses based on recommendations from the loss reduction study to use for tariff submissions.

1.4. CEB and LECO, in 2023, started the implementation of annual programs for women's empowerment based on WePOWER initiative, SLSEA obtained membership of WePOWER initiative and the Sri Lanka WePOWER National Chapter and commenced implementing similar programs.
11 Jul 2024 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-approves-support-power-sector-reforms-sri-lanka
2.1. PUCSL published and commenced implementation of a time-bound road map 2023-2025 for tariff reforms to implement cost-reflective electricity tariffs.
2.2. MOF off-loaded SLRs372 billion of debt repayable by CEB to the government in accordance with IMF agreements.

3.1. MOPE published and implemented new feed-in-tariffs for renewable energy power plants with environmental protection licenses under small power purchase agreements and rooftop solar installations to facilitate distributed renewable energy development to achieve 70% renewable energy target by 2030.

3.2. MOPE commenced monitoring of implementation (including the securing of environmental clearances) of the earlier-approved time-bound way forward road map 2023-2026 for integration of the private sector supported renewable energy development program into the national grid.
3.3. LECO and CEB implemented customer feedback mechanisms with equitable participation of female consumers, female entrepreneurs, and energy-sector CSOs focusing on women and disadvantaged groups.
